controls.label: Expected glow
controls.qualification: An estimate, not a measurement: black-body color at its published equilibrium temperature, 3,353 K.
controls.notes: Nobody has measured WASP-189 b's heat. This is the color of a black body at 3,353 K, the equilibrium temperature its paper computes from its star's light (Lendl et al. 2020, equilibrium temperature (NASA Exoplanet Archive planetary systems table)). On 120 hot Jupiters whose day side Spitzer measured, the measured temperature is within 20% of this kind of estimate for 83% (Deming et al. 2023). Its star lights the day side. Reflected starlight is not included.

charts.alt: The orbits of WASP-189's planets in this map from above, to scale, with WASP-189 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

WASP-189 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 1 sector (51) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 157910432, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, moved 12 minutes later to where TESS measures the dip, inside the published ephemeris's 3-sigma uncertainty of 17 minutes at these dates, then averaged in 17-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
